title: Nvidia’s real moat was never the chips. AI has started rewriting it.
excerpt: Nvidia’s dominance rests on CUDA, not just its chips. AI coding agents and the shift to inference are the first credible threats to that software moat.
content_html:
The usual story about Nvidia is a hardware story: the fastest chips, in the shortest supply, at the highest price. The more important part is software. For two decades the company’s real moat has been CUDA. It is the layer that turns its silicon into something developers can build AI on. That moat is now being tested.

CUDA, short for Compute Unified Device Architecture, took years to build. It bundles ready-made code and debugging tools. It also lets thousands of chips train a model together. The new threat is blunt: AI coding agents that can write that kind of low-level software themselves.

Jeremy Nixon is a former Google Brain researcher who founded the startup Infinity. He told Business Insider his team used agents to rebuild CUDA-like software for chip firm D-Matrix in about 10 hours. He framed it as proof that one of Nvidia’s biggest moats is being crossed.

Two moats, both under pressure

CUDA’s first advantage is the software. Its second is everything built on top of it. Millions of lines of company code and workflows make switching to a rival chip slow and costly. Amazon’s own documents once flagged CUDA as a major roadblock to adopting its in-house AI chips.

Agents chip away at the first advantage. The pressure is not only from startups. Google, Amazon and Microsoft have spent years writing software for their own chips. OpenAI and Anthropic have shown models that can generate system code. DeepSeek’s founder said coding agents, plus its own programming language, made building AI software much easier.

Nvidia does not dispute the trend so much as claim it. It says developers lean on CUDA’s libraries more every year. It also uses coding agents to build CUDA faster itself. The lock-in, in other words, may bend before it breaks.

The inference problem

The sharper threat is a shift in what AI chips are for. As the industry moves from training models to running them, priorities change. Buyers care less about peak performance and more about running AI cheaply. That favours software which works across different chips, not software welded to one vendor.

On the inference side, CUDA “is no longer a factor,” said Marshall Choy of Korean chip startup Rebellions. He calls it an open source play. It is the same opening our other inference challengers are chasing. Think optical chips, networking silicon, and Alibaba’s open-source alternative to CUDA itself.

Chris Lattner, whose startup Modular builds chip-agnostic AI software, says CUDA’s age cuts both ways. It carries years of legacy from its gaming origins, he says, “like Microsoft Windows trying to fit onto a phone.” Wall Street has noticed. Analysts read Nvidia’s flat stock over the past year as partly a bet against the moat.

The moat may just move

The counter-case is that agents relocate the moat rather than remove it. Generated code still has to be verified and optimised, and that is where CUDA’s ecosystem is deepest. Bing Xu, whose last chip-software startup was bought by Nvidia, argues that verification becomes the next moat.

“Agents can generate a lot of code in a short time, but verification is the biggest bottleneck,” Xu said. Lattner is blunter still. The hype, he says, is “very overblown.” Writing code is a small part of building software; the hard part is tuning it for production. And chip software is a niche field, with few public examples for agents to learn from.

So the honest read is not that CUDA is falling. It is that the thing protecting Nvidia has, for the first time, a plausible expiry date. Agents can now do in hours what used to take specialist teams years. Inference rewards whoever frees buyers from a single stack. Whether the moat holds comes down to one thing. Rivals must close the gap faster than Nvidia, which is “not sleeping,” can open a new one.

content_html_zh:
关于英伟达的通常故事是一个硬件故事：最快的芯片、最短的供应、最高的价格。 更重要的部分是软件。 二十年来，该公司真正的护城河一直是 CUDA。 正是这一层将其芯片变成了开发人员可以在其上构建人工智能的东西。 这条护城河现在正在接受测试。

CUDA 是计算统一设备架构的缩写，花了数年时间才构建出来。 它捆绑了现成的代码和调试工具。 它还可以让数千个芯片一起训练模型。 新的威胁是直截了当的：人工智能编码代理可以自己编写此类低级软件。

杰里米·尼克松 (Jeremy Nixon) 是前谷歌大脑研究员，创立了初创公司 Infinity。 他告诉 Business Insider，他的团队使用代理在大约 10 小时内为芯片公司 D-Matrix 重建了类似 CUDA 的软件。 他将此视为英伟达最大的护城河之一正在被跨越的证据。

两条护城河，都面临着压力

CUDA的第一个优势是软件。 第二个是建立在它之上的一切。 数百万行公司代码和工作流程使得切换到竞争对手芯片变得缓慢且成本高昂。 亚马逊自己的文件曾将 CUDA 标记为采用其内部人工智能芯片的主要障碍。

特工们逐渐蚕食了第一个优势。 压力不仅仅来自初创公司。 谷歌、亚马逊和微软花了数年时间为自己的芯片编写软件。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 展示了可以生成系统代码的模型。 DeepSeek 的创始人表示，编码代理加上自己的编程语言，使得构建人工智能软件变得更加容易。

英伟达并没有质疑这一趋势，而是声称它是这样的。 据称，开发人员对 CUDA 库的依赖逐年增加。 它还使用编码代理来更快地构建 CUDA。 换句话说，锁定在破裂之前可能会弯曲。

推理问题

更严重的威胁是人工智能芯片用途的转变。 随着行业从培训模式转向运行模式，优先事项发生了变化。 买家不太关心峰值性能，而更关心以低廉的成本运行人工智能。 这有利于在不同芯片上运行的软件，而不是焊接到一个供应商的软件。

韩国芯片初创公司 Rebellions 的 Marshall Choy 表示，在推理方面，CUDA“不再是一个因素”。 他称之为开源游戏。 这也是我们其他推理挑战者正在追逐的机会。 想想光学芯片、网络芯片和阿里巴巴 CUDA 本身的开源替代品。

Chris Lattner 的初创公司 Modular 开发了与芯片无关的 AI 软件，他表示 CUDA 的年龄是双向的。 他说，它继承了游戏起源多年的遗产，“就像微软 Windows 试图适应手机一样。” 华尔街已经注意到了。 分析师将英伟达过去一年的股价表现视为对护城河的押注。

护城河可能会移动

相反的情况是，特工们重新定位了护城河，而不是移除它。 生成的代码仍然需要验证和优化，而这正是 CUDA 生态系统最深入的地方。 Bing Xu 的最后一家芯片软件初创公司被 Nvidia 收购，他认为验证将成为下一个护城河。

“代理可以在短时间内生成大量代码，但验证是最大的瓶颈，”徐说。 拉特纳仍然比较直率。 他说，这种炒作“非常夸张”。 编写代码只是构建软件的一小部分；困难的部分是针对生产进行调整。 而芯片软件是一个小众领域，很少有公开的例子可供代理商学习。

所以诚实的解读并不是说 CUDA 正在下降。 这是保护 Nvidia 的东西第一次有了一个合理的有效期。 过去专家团队需要花费数年时间才能完成的工作现在只需数小时即可完成。 推理会奖励那些将买家从单一堆栈中解放出来的人。 护城河是否稳固取决于一件事。 竞争对手必须比“不睡觉”的英伟达更快地缩小差距，才能打开新的差距。
